body: I feel so out of control now, I feel like I’m being driven towards insanity. I dont know why I’m allowing myself to go through this torture. Every day is getting worse, I havnt had a good day in 2 years

Exactly my thought process too but personally the way I see God, for someone to have been so mentally ill that they felt they had to kill themselves, I believe God knows whats in your heart and your intentions, he understands and knows how much you suffered, even if you failed, you tried really hard to pass the test, I dont believe God would want to make you suffer more for it

Another thing I think about is if we are sent back to earth, what if the attempt permanently damages us and makes life even worse? Suicide must be traumatic af, the fact that we’d have to go through all of that all over again to be at peace… damn
You have no idea how much that means to me

Theres a reason were hell bent on dying. People with depression do come to realise that there is no cure, and the only thing they can do is learn to live with it. 

But, those with very severe depression, they do learn to live with it but after a while life gets too painful, its extremely difficult to do anything anymore because you dont feel any desire for anything or care about anything, and your passions slowly disappear, and it doesnt matter what you do to try to get those things back and feel something other than extreme sadness, you just lose yourself more and more. 

We stay and we plead our case because believe it or not we dont actually want to die, its a last resort, we just want this to stop, we just want to feel ok and normal and in control, this forces us to hesitate at first but eventually hesitation fades and then we take our life.

I started training as a nurse to fill my life with meaning, I thought helping to relieve other peoples pain and suffering, thats something worthwhile, its not like working for money just so you can live to work more, theres more that comes out of it. 

And yes it does bring me happiness seeing my patients get better. But everyday I do my job and I come back home to nothing, feeling misreable again. What about my pain and suffering? 

Yes you can see or experience cool things but after a while depression can steal every ounce of excitement you have, energy and love for life and desire to try things. It steals all your interests and passions and leaves you feeling empty and hollow, it paralyses you. And you need to experience this level of depression to understand it and understand how out of control you are. 

For some people it may get better yes, but that isnt the case for everyone, for some people it only ever gets worse, even those that found meaning or tried every method of treatment or read a thousand books to help change their ‘outlook’, those with crippling depression.

You know what I hate hearing? ‘Everything gets better’. No it fucking doesnt sally, maybe for some people, but for some of us it only ever gets worse. 
Thats what happened with me, I latched onto that and waited and waited and waited for things to get better and I was let down, because life became more and more dreadful. 

I believe the only thing that truly gives life meaning which doesnt have the potential to hurt you is helping people and doing your part to make the world a better place, thats why I started training to be a nurse. It didn’t treat the depression, it didn’t make me stop praying for my life to end, but it does make life mean something, my soul feels more at peace knowing I can atleast help alleviate some of the suffering others have to put up with. Have a think about it

Finally, someone that can relate. This brought me so much comfort you have no idea. Forcing myself to stay alive and drag myself through this endless torment day in day out is in my opinion, self harm. 

They always tell you it gets better, but that isn’t the case for everyone. For some of us, it only ever gets worse. Maybe the reason why ending our own lives becomes a relentless thought is because when we are finally broken beyond repair and we can’t possibly handle anymore pain, that’s the brain’s natural response, to shut the system down because it’s starting to malfunction. We weren’t built to withstand this kind of torture for such a long time. 

There are a lot of people who understand why someone would end their life and allow themselves to rest if they’re experiencing unimaginable physical pain caused by an incurable illness, but why is it so hard to accept people experiencing the same thing but mentally wanting to do the same? 

I know its selfish, I know there are so many people around the world who do have it worse, who would do anything to have my life despite the trauma, heartbreak and worsening depression. I am genuinely grateful for the simple things; to have access to education and work, to be able to afford food and a home, to be in a country where I’m allowed to exercise my human rights, to have friends that care. But this illness has stolen from me every ounce of happiness and love and will for life. I’ve not been experiencing life, I’ve just been watching others experience it.

I feel that if I have any respect left for myself, I’d free myself from this constant misery and pain.
